equation_request.abstract:
We propose a scheme for perfect transfer of an unknown qubit state via the discrete-time quantum walk on a line or a circle. For this purpose, we introduce an additional coin operator which is applied at the end of the walk. This operator does not depend on the state to be transferred. We show that perfect state transfer over an arbitrary distance can be achieved only if the walk is driven by an identity or a flip coin operator. Other biased coin operators and Hadamard coin allow perfect state transfer over finite distances only. Furthermore, we show that quantum walks ending with a perfect state transfer are periodic.

January 2015

specification.problem: Perfect transfer of an unknown single-qubit (coin) state from one site of a discrete-time quantum walk (DTQW) on a line or a circle to another site, using a state-independent coin operator applied once at the end of the walk; characterise which driving coins allow transfer over arbitrary vs. finite distances and show that such walks are periodic.
specification.reconstruction_scope: ONE smallest useful construction (chosen here as an assumption, no experiment_scope was supplied): a DTQW on a circle of N = 4 sites driven by the identity coin, transferring the coin state alpha|0> + beta|1> from site x_0 = 0 to site d = 2 in t = 2 steps, with the final coin operator reducing to the identity in the chosen shift convention. The generic DTQW definitions and the abstract's perfect-state-transfer (PST) and periodicity conditions are stated in general form. Outside scope: the paper's explicit final coin operator C_f for Hadamard and general biased coins, the finite-distance results for those coins, the line (infinite lattice) analysis, the flip-coin case, and the general proof of periodicity.

symbols.meaning: Coin Hilbert space spanned by |0\rangle, |1\rangle (one qubit)

symbols.domain: \mathbb{C}^N for a circle of N sites (x \in \mathbb{Z}_N); \ell^2(\mathbb{Z}) for a line

symbols.meaning: Number of sites of the circle
symbols.domain: positive even integer; N = 4 in the chosen instance

symbols.meaning: Transfer distance (receiver site is x_0 + d)
symbols.domain: positive integer; d = 2 in the instance

symbols.meaning: Number of walk steps before the final coin operator
symbols.domain: positive integer; t = 2 in the instance

symbols.meaning: Driving coin operator applied at every step
symbols.domain: U(2); C = I in the instance

symbols.meaning: Additional state-independent coin operator applied once at the end of the walk
One step of the walk, U = S (C \otimes I_p)
Unknown amplitudes of the qubit state to be transferred

equations.label: Conditional shift operator
equations.latex: S = |0\rangle\langle 0| \otimes \sum_{x} |x-1\rangle\langle x| + |1\rangle\langle 1| \otimes \sum_{x} |x+1\rangle\langle x|, \quad x \pm 1 \text{ taken mod } N \text{ on the circle}
equations.description: Coin state |0> moves the walker one site to the left, |1> one site to the right; on the circle positions are reduced modulo N, on the line x ranges over all integers.
equations.justification: Standard definition of the DTQW shift on a line/cycle; the abstract only names the walk, not this convention.
assumptions: Direction convention (|0> left, |1> right) is a choice; the paper's convention may differ (an equivalent flip of coin labels).
Position labels on the circle are integers mod N.

equations.label: Walk step and t-step evolution
equations.description: Each step applies the driving coin C to the coin register, then the conditional shift; the walk runs for t steps.
equations.justification: Standard DTQW evolution; the abstract refers to the walk being 'driven by' a coin operator.
assumptions: Coin is applied before the shift in each step (standard ordering).

equations.label: Initial state carrying the unknown qubit
equations.description: The unknown qubit state is encoded in the coin register and the walker is localised at the sender site x_0.
equations.abstract_quote: perfect transfer of an unknown qubit state via the discrete-time quantum walk
equations.justification: Inferred: the only qubit degree of freedom in a DTQW is the coin, so the unknown state must be encoded in the coin with the walker localised at a sender site.
assumptions: Walker initially localised at a single site x_0.

equations.label: Perfect state transfer condition with final coin operator
equations.description: Exact equality up to a global phase, required for all input amplitudes; C_f must not depend on alpha, beta. This defines perfect transfer over distance d after t steps.
equations.abstract_quote: we introduce an additional coin operator which is applied at the end of the walk. This operator does not depend on the state to be transferred.
equations.justification: Formalises the abstract's statement that a state-independent coin operator applied after the walk completes the perfect transfer; the explicit form of C_f for general coins is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Global phase phi is allowed (standard for perfect state transfer).
Receiver site is x_0 + d (mod N on the circle).

equations.label: Identity-coin walk on an N-cycle and transfer to the antipodal site (chosen instance)
equations.latex: U^{t}|\psi_{\mathrm{in}}\rangle = \alpha\,|0\rangle\otimes|x_0 - t \bmod N\rangle + \beta\,|1\rangle\otimes|x_0 + t \bmod N\rangle; \quad t = d = N/2,\ C_f = I \Rightarrow (\alpha|0\rangle+\beta|1\rangle)\otimes|x_0 + N/2\rangle
equations.description: With C = I the two coin components travel in opposite directions without mixing; on a circle of even N they recombine exactly at the antipodal site after N/2 steps, giving perfect transfer over distance d = N/2 with trivial final coin. Instance: N = 4, x_0 = 0, t = d = 2.
equations.justification: Direct consequence of eq_1-eq_3 for C = I; chosen as the smallest exactly verifiable instance consistent with the abstract's claim that the identity coin allows transfer over arbitrary distance (here by choosing N = 2d). The paper's own setting for the identity/flip coins (line vs circle, shift convention) is not stated in the abstract.
assumptions: In this shift convention C_f = I; in a flip-flop shift convention the roles of identity and flip coins interchange.

equations.label: Periodicity of a walk ending with perfect state transfer
equations.latex: \exists\, T \in \mathbb{Z}_{>0}: \quad U^{T}|\psi_{\mathrm{in}}\rangle = e^{i\theta}|\psi_{\mathrm{in}}\rangle; \qquad \text{instance: } C = I,\ N = 4 \Rightarrow U^{4} = I_c \otimes I_p
equations.description: The abstract claims walks that end with PST are periodic; for the instance the identity-coin walk on the 4-cycle returns exactly to the initial state after T = N = 4 steps (shift by ±4 is the identity).
equations.abstract_quote: we show that quantum walks ending with a perfect state transfer are periodic.
equations.justification: Formalises the abstract's periodicity claim; the general proof and general period are not available, only the instance value T = N is verifiable from eq_5.
assumptions: Periodicity is taken as return of the walker state up to a global phase.
General period T for other coins unknown.

registers.name: coin
registers.role: Carries the unknown qubit state alpha|0> + beta|1>; acted on by C each step and by C_f at the end.

registers.name: position
registers.role: Walker position x in Z_N, encoded as a 2-bit integer (|x> = |x_1 x_0> with x = 2 x_1 + x_0); shifted by ±1 mod N conditioned on the coin.

steps.description: Prepare the coin register in the unknown state alpha|0> + beta|1> and the position register in |x_0> = |0> (binary |00>).
Apply t = 2 walk steps U = S (C ⊗ I) with C = I: each step is a controlled decrement (coin |0>) / controlled increment (coin |1>) of the position modulo N = 4.
Apply the final state-independent coin operator C_f (equal to the identity for this instance) to the coin register, completing the perfect transfer to site x_0 + d = 2.
(Optional check of periodicity) Continue for a total of T = 4 steps and verify return to the initial state.

specification.measurement: For verification only (not part of the transfer protocol): measure the position register in the computational basis, expecting outcome x = 2 (|10>) with probability 1; then characterise the coin register (e.g. state tomography for several test inputs alpha, beta, or inverse-preparation and measurement of |0>) to confirm it equals alpha|0> + beta|1>.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate the position-outcome probability at site d and the coin fidelity F = |<psi_target|rho_coin|psi_target>| from measurement statistics; perfect transfer corresponds to position probability 1 and F = 1 for all test inputs.
assumptions: No experiment_scope was supplied; the instance (circle, N = 4, identity coin, x_0 = 0, d = 2, t = 2, C_f = I) was chosen as the smallest exactly verifiable construction and is not taken from the paper.
Standard DTQW conventions (coin-then-shift, |0> moves left, |1> moves right, positions mod N) are assumed; the paper's conventions may differ.
Perfect transfer is defined up to a global phase.
The identity-coin instance makes the paper's additional final coin operator trivial; the nontrivial C_f relevant for Hadamard/biased coins is not reconstructed.
missing_information: Explicit form of the final coin operator C_f for the Hadamard coin and general biased coins, and the finite distances/step numbers at which they achieve perfect transfer.

The paper's precise setting (line vs circle, shift convention, initial state) under which both identity and flip coins yield transfer over arbitrary distance; in the convention used here the flip coin with a standard shift yields a period-2 walk without transfer, suggesting a different convention in the paper.
General proof and expression for the period T of walks ending with perfect state transfer.
Definition and treatment of perfect transfer on the infinite line, where the two coin components of identity/flip-coin walks never recombine in the convention used here.
